definitions.explanation: A lord or ruler in feudal Japan. Also used figuratively to describe someone who acts in an authoritative or pampered manner.

examples.japanese: {殿様|とのさま}は{供|とも}を{連|つ}れて{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: The lord set out on a journey with his retainers.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{殿様|とのさま}は{大|おお}きな{城|しろ}に{住|す}んでいた。
examples.english: Feudal lords in the Edo period lived in large castles.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{殿様|とのさま}{商売|しょうばい}で{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: He failed because of his haughty business approach.
examples.notes: 殿様商売: doing business in a lordly, complacent manner; not making an effort to attract customers

notes:
{殿様|とのさま} was the respectful title for feudal lords ({大名|だいみょう}) in Japan. Today it is used in historical contexts and figuratively to describe someone who acts entitled or pampered.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {殿様|とのさま}{商売|しょうばい}: lordly/complacent business style (not trying to attract customers)
- {殿様|とのさま}ガエル: Japanese tree frog (literally 'lord frog')
- {殿様|とのさま}{気分|きぶん}: feeling like a lord (being pampered)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Frequently appears in {時代劇|じだいげき} (historical dramas) and children's stories about feudal Japan. The image of {殿様|とのさま} is of someone powerful but sometimes comically detached from everyday life.

RELATED WORDS:
- {大名|だいみょう}: feudal lord (historical/formal term)
- {武士|ぶし}: samurai, warrior
- {家来|けらい}: retainer, vassal
